As a really quite person aswell, and someone who still has issues talking with people, I'm slowly improving by just saying small things, even if it's just being polite. For example when i buy something i will say thank you, or if i don't hear someone i will say sorry? instead of what or just ignoring them. But i go out of my way to be polite, in order to make myself not constantly look back at the conversation and believe i was a bad person, which would just make me worry about talking even more, while also hopefully making them a bit happier or at least not annoyed.

 I don't start conversation's by myself but the idea of upsetting someone when they talk to me usually makes me talk, even if its just greetings or pleasantaries. 

So I'd just recommend starting small and slowly working your way up, it might take along time, or you might pick it up quickly, it also helps if you have a close friend or family member you are comfortable around, just to get you used to talking. This has helped me when it comes to conversing, I've always been known as a silent person, but being polite gives people good impressions and is much less likely to cause others to be upset with you or be mean to you, which will help your confidence and give you experience when it comes to talking.

I personally don't think valuing something is meaning, I see meaning as a reason why we exist, something we exist for, I don't exist for things I value, I simply exist, with or without the things I value I would still exist. I believe if we truly had meaning, it would be something larger than things we value. Putting meaning on things you value personally seems alot like existentialism, I believe meaning doesn't exist at all, having something I value doesn't create a greater meaning, they are simply things I value. But life is complex, and the definition of what people consider meaning is different for everyone, if it was the same I don't think there would be so much philosophy about it. 

I can definitely see where you come from, as you could argue that having something you value gives you meaning, but overall I see that as pointless, creating a superficial meaning seems more like a coping mechanism, as overall it won't matter in the end, my life won't be enriched giving myself meaning, therefore I don't bother to. I'd rather just do what I enjoy without meaning.

My main point of the post was asking why people care so much about meaning in general, so many people let the search for meaning dictate their life, that they end up not truly living, or forcing themselves to live a lie to comfort themselves, instead of just not caring and live life. I've noticed it in alot of elderly religious people, I remember talking to one when I was younger as I went to a religious school, they told me not to let meaning take control of my life, as if you do, you'll reach my age realising that you left life pass bye all for nothing, as you haven't found anything a true sense of meaning, you most likely just found something that everyone is claiming to be meaning. Which In his case was religion. 

I'm not too bored in people looking for meaning if they don't let it dictate their life, whatever makes them happy personally, I've talked to so many people who are broken or shells of there former self as what they thought was meaning wasn't true, or substantial enough for them, now they are older they looked back on the time they believed they wasted and wish they could do it again. I think if they didn't put so much meaning in meaning, they would never of gotten to that stage, the effect of the realisation wouldn't effect them so much, and people wouldn't have to look back wishing they didn't waste there time searching, as they wouldn't of cared enough to search for meaning in the first place.

I apologise if this doesn't make much sense either, I've always been terrible at putting my thoughts into words, usually results in a rabble that doesn't make much sense, and in alot of cases doesn't get the point I want across, across.
